title: FAMOS: Feed-Forward 3D Articulation Modeling from Sparse Observations
why_read: A feed-forward model for inferring how 3D objects with movable parts are jointed, based on sparse point-cloud views.
analysis: FAMOS predicts which parts of an object move and how their joints work, using a small set of unordered partial point clouds rather than requiring a full 3D scan or a fixed number of views. It uses a transformer architecture that attends both within individual observations and across all of them jointly, plus a training objective that rewards using the motion evidence spread across multiple views. The authors also built a synthetic data generator to work around limited real-world datasets for this task. The results show improvements over both other feed-forward approaches and slower optimization-based ones, making it relevant to robotics and 3D asset creation pipelines that need to understand articulated objects like drawers, doors, or hinges.
